template/html_library#

Named HTML templates, for partials.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let library = HtmlTemplateLibrary(["header": HtmlTemplate("<h1>{{title}}</h1>")]);
library.template("header");

Description#

Named HTML templates, for partials.

Names are exact: no trimming or case folding. template/engine's TemplatePartials is the one library of the engine (#178); SectionTemplate turns a TemplateLibrary into it.

object HtmlTemplateLibrary#

object HtmlTemplateLibrary

Immutable ordered library, empty by default. Sequence constructors snapshot size once then each ascending item once, rejecting invalid size/excess count before item access. Optional nonnegative maximum_templates defaults to 1024; zero permits an empty source. Duplicates are checked after the full snapshot. Original source failures propagate; no cursor/first/last/close calls. Queries never revisit the source. Missing names throw MissingHtmlTemplate, while membership returns false, including for "". Returned values/names outlive us. Retains HtmlTemplate owners; no resource acquisition, compilation or destroy. O(n) references; duplicates and lookups go through a map of names (#178). The count does not limit source bytes; flat HtmlTemplate owns its limits. Composition will apply explicit aggregate limits to these typed source values. Only HtmlTemplate is accepted; no plain TextTemplate or arbitrary source role. Contract: docs/std/template-html-library-guide.md. Example: HtmlTemplateLibrary(NamedHtmlTemplate("greeting",HtmlTemplate("Hello"))); HTML partial expansion is separate: this module only names typed templates. Run: okkama run -t std/template/html_library.ok
